significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(ii) causal conclusion that an internal "evaluation-awareness feature causally raises the refusal-direction projection" and thereby inflates harmful-prompt refusal, establishing both a framing-dependent behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism for that single behavior. This would constrain explanations of benchmark/deployment refusal gaps by decomposing observed refusal into an evaluation-conditioned component and a residual component, but it remains the bounded "separable direction + causal role + steering repair" pattern rather than a law predicting multiple behaviors or configurations. SAD (Laine et al., 2024) operationalizes situational awareness and Arditi et al. (2024) treats refusal as causally manipulable, so a positive result would connect two quantities used in safety analysis; a controlled negative would meaningfully rule out their proposed causal coupling rather than merely report failure to decode a feature, although it would not exclude other forms of test-taking. In the topic-substitution check, generic mechanistic work on LLM safety would not earn this score; the specific evaluation-awareness/refusal decomposition makes the claim sharper than the obvious refusal-direction hypothesis, but its single-behavior bound keeps it near the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handles are the measurable "eval-inflation gap" and the "cheap 'deployment-framing' probe to de-bias safety benchmarks," which evaluators could use before deployment to flag when benchmark refusal may be inflated, providing ex-ante lead time rather than only explaining a failure afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the hypothesis predicts a transferable relation—greater evaluation-awareness should raise refusal projection and suppressing it should increase harmful compliance—rather than supplying only an uncommitted procedure for searching for a direction. The asserted scope covers LLM safety benchmarks and multiple model/checkpoint classes, and downstream users include safety auditors who compare or gate models, though simulated deployment framing limits how directly the handle supports real deployment decisions. The topic-substitution check lowers generic "safer through interpretability" work to the median; the specific pre-deployment audit metric, causal interpretation, and evaluator uptake support the higher reach score.
